title: bs2026-resolution: reproducibility artifacts for the input-resolution and edge-deployment study
description:
Data manifests, aggregated results and analysis code for a study of input resolution in bird species identification on an edge device (14 input resolutions x 6 architectures x 2 training regimes x 30 seeds = 2,520 checkpoints and 5,040 evaluation conditions, with on-device measurements on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano 8 GB).

The images themselves are not redistributed. Published instead is one row per image (12,519 rows) giving the source, identifier, URL, SHA-256, group identifier under two grouping rules, and membership in both the image-wise and the group-disjoint split, so that the same image set can be reassembled from the original sources under their own licences. SHA-256 is given for all 12,519 images and 5,756 carry a directly resolvable URL.

Also included: both split definitions, every aggregate the paper's tables and figures are built from, the training, evaluation, aggregation and figure-generation code, and the Jetson-side scripts for ONNX export, graph splitting, TensorRT builds and latency and accuracy measurement.
